messages:
sam: quick flag — noticed missing token-level latency for kvcache on the rw-token dashboard after last night's kernel-selector rollout :eyes:
anya: which metric keys are missing?
sam: token_latency.kvcache.* series are gone for ~03:40–04:15 UTC, shows as zeros across the histogram heatmap
lee: saw an alert for downstream per-route KPIs too (route=user-chat -> p95 spiked but token breakdown empty)
kevin: could be statsd emitter choking on high-cardinality tags from the new kernel selector. we changed kernel_tag from low-cardinality -> runtime_variant_id in the rollout
anya: do we have any evidence in the OTLP pipeline? maybe an exporter error or dropped_count?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout "kernel-selector-v2" to prod completed at 2024-12-07T03:38:12Z
kevin: pulled logs from statsd-exporter pods — saw multiple `write error: broken pipe` and `max_datagram_size` warnings around the same window
sam: pasted a short snippet from exporter stderr:
```
2024-12-07T03:39:03Z statsd-exporter[1]: warn: dropping metric line (too many tags): token_latency.kvcache|h|#model:ggml-tiny,route:user-chat,runtime_variant_id:rv-2024-12-07-1
```
lee: that matches — runtime_variant_id exploded cardinality. OTel ingesters show sporadic sampling too (span attr filters hit)
anya: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back kernel_tag to low-cardinality 2) add a tag-filter at statsd-exporter to drop runtime_variant_id for histogram metrics 3) run a backfill for dropped metrics
sam: prefer not to rollback the selector yet — it's giving better tail latency overall. propose option 2 + backfill
kevin: I can add a simple regex filter on the emitter: `drop_tags: {"token_latency.kvcache": ["runtime_variant_id"]}` and deploy now
lee: need to coordinate backfill window and tooling. backfill plan: reprocess raw OTLP/ingest logs from s3 for 03:30–04:30 UTC, reconstruct histogram buckets, and re-emit to metrics DB with a special tag `backfill=true` so dashboards can join
anya: estimate for the backfill run? we have ~300M events in that hour for kvcache-heavy hosts
lee: with current tooling (kafka -> spark preprocess) ~6 hours if we run at normal parallelism; can be cut to ~90m with burst parallelism on staging cluster
sam: short term: kevin deploy the tag filter, add statsd exporter rate-limit guard and alert on exported-drops > 0; ops: run canary for 10% hosts for 15m
kevin: deploying filter now, will post status
kevin: deployed to canary pods at 03:58 UTC, emitter logs show `filtered 1.2k lines` then export resumed :thumbsup:
anya: dashboards show token_latency.kvcache returning for canary hosts, overall cluster still missing until full rollout
sam: can we schedule the backfill off-hours and gate it by a quick smoke test? we should also add a compensating metric in the pipeline: `metrics_ingest.overrun{stage:statsd-exporter}`
lee: I'll prepare the Spark job and the re-emit job. aiming to run at 22:00 UTC with burst parallelism (requires approval for ephemeral nodes)
kevin: created PR for statsd exporter config and alerting: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 (cc @anya for review)
anya: reviewing now. also adding a temporary dashboard panel that overlays `metrics_ingest.overrun` with `token_latency.kvcache.count` so we can confirm backfill coverage
sam: decision notes: do not rollback kernel selector; deploy tag-filter to exporter; run 22:00 UTC backfill with `backfill=true`; create incident note and postmortem if counts don't reconcile within 48h
ops-bot: incident-bot: incident created (INC-2024-12207) — metrics-drop-kvcache — severity:medium
lee: once backfill completes, we should re-run a quick eval against a held prompt set to make sure token-level latency distributions align with pre-rollout baseline
kevin: canary to full rollout started at 04:10 UTC, exporter logs show no further drops after filter applied
anya: thanks all — follow-ups: kevin merge + full rollout, lee run backfill + smoke, sam write short incident note and link dashboards.
sam: I'll post updates in #incidents and close the thread when backfill final counts OK :party_parrot:
kevin: tagging @oncall for awareness
